Test observed genotype counts for Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium

Source: R/hwe_diagnostic.R
hwe_test.Rd

Test one biallelic autosomal locus using counts of diploid individuals. The null is Hardy-Weinberg proportions with an unknown allele frequency. Pearson inference estimates that frequency from the counts. Exact inference conditions on the allele total. A large p-value does not establish equilibrium.

Usage

hwe_test(counts, method = c("exact", "chisq"))

Arguments

counts

Numeric vector of three nonnegative whole counts, in 0, 1, and 2 copies of the same counted allele. If named, use "0", "1", and "2" in that order. The sum must be positive and no larger than 2^52.

method

One of "exact" (default) or "chisq" (uncorrected Pearson).

Value

A list with N, counts, observed_probs, allele_frequency, expected_probs, expected_counts, Pearson statistic and df, the selected method and its p_value, the signed heterozygote deficit F = 1 - observed/expected, and sparse_expected indicating any expected count below five. Negative F indicates heterozygote excess. The Pearson degrees of freedom describe statistic, even when the selected p-value is exact.

Details

The uncorrected Pearson statistic has an asymptotic chi-square reference distribution with one degree of freedom: three cells minus one total-count constraint and one estimated allele frequency. Expected counts below five prompt a warning for Pearson inference. The two-sided exact p-value conditions on the observed allele count and sums the probabilities of tables at least as unlikely as the observed table, including ties (Wigginton et al., 2005). Exact enumeration is limited to one million conditional tables. At a monomorphic locus there is one conditional table (exact p-value 1) and no regular Pearson test. The function warns and returns NA for the Pearson statistic, degrees of freedom, and F.

References

Wigginton JE, Cutler DJ, Abecasis GR (2005). A note on exact tests of Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. American Journal of Human Genetics 76(5), 887-893. doi:10.1086/429864 .

See also

hwe_power(), hwe_mssn()

Examples

hwe_test(c(88, 10, 2))
#> $N
#> [1] 100
#> 
#> $counts
#>  0  1  2 
#> 88 10  2 
#> 
#> $observed_probs
#>    0    1    2 
#> 0.88 0.10 0.02 
#> 
#> $allele_frequency
#> [1] 0.07
#> 
#> $expected_probs
#>      0      1      2 
#> 0.8649 0.1302 0.0049 
#> 
#> $expected_counts
#>     0     1     2 
#> 86.49 13.02  0.49 
#> 
#> $statistic
#> [1] 5.380119
#> 
#> $df
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $method
#> [1] "exact"
#> 
#> $p_value
#> [1] 0.06544427
#> 
#> $F
#> [1] 0.2319508
#> 
#> $sparse_expected
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
hwe_test(c(40, 30, 30), method = "chisq")
#> $N
#> [1] 100
#> 
#> $counts
#>  0  1  2 
#> 40 30 30 
#> 
#> $observed_probs
#>   0   1   2 
#> 0.4 0.3 0.3 
#> 
#> $allele_frequency
#> [1] 0.45
#> 
#> $expected_probs
#>      0      1      2 
#> 0.3025 0.4950 0.2025 
#> 
#> $expected_counts
#>     0     1     2 
#> 30.25 49.50 20.25 
#> 
#> $statistic
#> [1] 15.51882
#> 
#> $df
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $method
#> [1] "chisq"
#> 
#> $p_value
#> [1] 8.16877e-05
#> 
#> $F
#> [1] 0.3939394
#> 
#> $sparse_expected
#> [1] FALSE
#>
